overview.body:
**Hebe** ​(*hebe*) ‌— Youth, ‌Cupbearer ​· ​Youth ​(from ἥβη) ​— ​belongs ‌to ​the Greek ​tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under ‌the ​domain "Youth, ​Cupbearer". ​The ​name ​means "Youth ‌(from ​ἥβη)".

‌**Hebe** ​is youth, ‌cupbearer. ​The ‌name ​means "Youth ‌(from ​ἥβη)" ​and ‌belongs to ‌the ‌greek ​tradition.

PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name ​as **Hebe** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/hebe/). ​The ​original carries ​both ​stress ‌and ‌vowel length, ​and ‌exactly ​one historically ​valid ‌Unicode ‌restoration ‌exists, which ‌places ​the ‌name ​in Tier ​1. ​The ‌plain ​ASCII form ​*hebe* ​survives ‌as ​a modern ​convenience ​imposed ‌by ​the early ‌domain-name ​system; ‌the restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, ​is the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
The ​name ‌is attested ‌in ​Greek ​as ​**Ἥβη**. Etymologically ​it ​means ‌"Youth ​(from ἥβη)".

​The ‌ASCII ​form ‌*hebe* ​survives only ‌because ​the ​early ​domain-name system ​could ​not ‌carry ​diacritics; it ‌is ​a ‌technological ​compromise, not ‌an ​ancient ‌spelling. ​The Unicode ​restoration ‌**Hebe** ‌recovers ‌the ​full diacritic ​detail ‌of ​the ​scholarly transliteration ‌directly ​in ​the ‌address bar. ​The ‌original ​carries ​both stress ​and ​vowel ‌length, ‌and exactly ​one ‌historically ​valid ​Unicode ‌restoration exists, ‌which ‌places ‌the ​name in ‌Tier ​1.

​The ​letter-by-letter transformation ‌runs:

​- ​**h** ​→ **H** ‌— ​Rough ​breathing
​- **e** ‌→ ​**e** ‌— ​Short ‌epsilon
- ​**b** ‌→ ‌**b** ​— Beta
​- ​**e** ​→ ‌**e** — ‌Short ​epsilon

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/hebe/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**hebe** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Hebe.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"hebe" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Hebe".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"hebe" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Hebe" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Hebe was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Hebe ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Hebe ‌place ​youth, cupbearer ​at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living mythological ​world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Hebe ‌appears ​in greek ‌tradition ​as youth, ​cupbearer. ​The ​name's meaning, ​"Youth ‌(from ​ἥβη)", shapes ‌the ​narratives told ‌about ​this ‌figure.

### ​Worship ‌and ​Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ‌and later ‌tradition-keepers ‌preserved ​Hebe in ​ritual, ‌text, ​and iconography, ​ensuring ‌the name ​survived ​into ‌the modern ​scholarly ‌record.

​The myths ​of ​Hebe survive ​in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, and ​later ‌retellings. ​Each version ​reflects ‌the interests ‌of ‌its ‌tellers — ​poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does ​not privilege ​a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Hebe ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Hebe ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Greek ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Ἥβη, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​youth ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Hebe is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of youth, ​Cupbearer ‌in ​the ​mind ‌and to ​ask ‌what ​of ‌it endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"Youth ​(from ἥβη)" ‌— ​and ‌a ​name that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​youth, ‌Cupbearer ​· ​Youth ‌(from ἥβη).

​Sit ‌with ​the ​restored ​form — ​Hebe ‌— ‌and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ​become ​the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ‌a ​small ‌act ​of attention, ​a ​refusal ‌to ​let the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form ​*hebe* ​stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
